The Mother of God Koukouzelissa

Theotokos

The Mother of God Koukouzelissa

Kukuzelissa · Koukouzelis icon

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 1:46–49

King James Version · Scripture previews

The OCA names the Koukouzelissa after the Athonite singer John Koukouzelis and locates it at the Great Lavra.

[1] Published source,paragraph 3; Published source,paragraph 8

What is depicted

The selected file identifies a twelfth-century Athonite icon. A richly worked metal covering surrounds the faces of Mary and the Child; the record’s date describes this image rather than proving the date of the later miracle narrative.

[2] Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field title; Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.ImageDescription; Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.DateTimeOriginal; Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Artist; Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Credit; Exact file record File:Mother of God the Kukuzelissa.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.LicenseShortName

History and tradition

The published life describes the former court singer’s monastic life and singing in the Lavra’s choir. After an Akathist, he dreams of Mary encouraging him and giving him a coin. The account says that the coin was placed beneath the icon and that healings were later attributed to it and the image. The episode is identified as hagiographic tradition.

[1] Published source,paragraph 3; Published source,paragraph 4; Published source,paragraph 8

Published explanation

The OCA connects the title with the hymnographer’s memory and records October 1 and the tenth Friday after Pascha as commemorations. The movable reference is retained as printed, without constructing a new universal calendar rule or identifying every copy as the original.

[1] Published source,paragraph 8

And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,

And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.

For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.

For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.

Related biblical song of Mary; not a quotation from John Koukouzelis.

[3] Luke 1:46–49
